components.css: :host { --main-color: #237a57; --main-color-rgb: 35, 122, 87; --color-two: #c6e45a; --black-color: #191919; --black-color-rgb: 25, 25, 25; --white-color: #ffffff; } .ds-btn { position: relative; display: inline-block; overflow: hidden; padding: 16px 34px; border-radius: 50px; font-family: "Manrope", sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 15px; text-transform: capitalize; text-decoration: none; color: #fff; background-color: #237a57; background-image: linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(35, 122, 87, 1) 0%, rgba(198, 228, 90, 1) 100%); } .ds-btn::before { content: ""; position: absolute; width: 200%; height: 200%; top: -200%; left: 50%; transform: translateX(-50%); border-radius: 50%; z-index: 1; background-image: linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(198, 228, 90, 1) 0%, rgba(35, 122, 87, 1) 100%); transition: top 800ms; } .ds-btn:hover::before { top: -40%; } .ds-btn-wrap { position: relative; z-index: 2; display: inline-block; overflow: hidden; vertical-align: top; } .ds-btn-one, .ds-btn-two { display: block; transition: all 0.3s ease; } .ds-btn-two { position: absolute; top: 100%; } .ds-btn:hover .ds-btn-one { transform: translateY(-150%); } .ds-btn:hover .ds-btn-two { top: 50%; transform: translateY(-50%); } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #237a57; outline-offset: 3px; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-btn::before, .ds-btn-one, .ds-btn-two { transition: none; } }

narrative.overview:
Creative North Star: "The Greenhouse Studio"

TechFiyr's site reads like a glasshouse where products are grown: a deep forest green flows into a fresh lime, and that 90° gradient is the brand's signature, spent on the elements that ask for action (buttons, the preloader, section-title dots, carousel arrows). The frames around it are soft and very round, like curved glass panes. Hero and page-title photos sit in a 50px rounded frame inset 20px from the viewport, CTAs and service cards are 150px capsules, and icons sit in circles. The mood is fresh, confident and approachable: bold Outfit headings carry the confidence, and the round geometry and lively hover motion keep it friendly.

Depth comes from contrast before it comes from shadow. White content sections alternate with near-black feature blocks and a black-to-charcoal footer, and page-title photos sit under a 70% navy wash with one giant outlined Raleway word behind the heading. Density is generous: about 120px of vertical rhythm between sections on desktop, a 1320px container, and plenty of air around each heading.

Motion belongs to the personality. Button labels swap on hover while a reversed gradient sweeps up behind them, nav labels roll, service-card icons spin, cards lift, a marquee band scrolls, odometer counters tick and the back-to-top ring fills. All of it switches off under prefers-reduced-motion.

The concept is fixed. New work extends this world; it does not redesign it.
keyCharacteristics: Forest-green → lime 90° gradient as the single brand signature
Very round geometry: 50px pills and frames, 150px capsules, circular icons
Navy-washed photo heroes with a giant outlined word
Uppercase green eyebrow flanked by three pulsing gradient dots
Lively, tactile hover motion, always with a reduced-motion fallback

rules.name: The Gradient Signature Rule
rules.body: The forest → lime 90° gradient (linear-gradient(90deg, #237a57 0%, #c6e45a 100%)) is the brand mark. Its hover state is the same gradient reversed (lime → forest). It goes on action and identity elements, never on body text or headings.

rules.name: The Lime Is Never Ink Rule
rules.body: Fresh Lime never appears as text on a light background, and small white text never sits over the lime end of the gradient.

rules.name: The Marketplace Quarantine Rule
rules.body: Marketplace Green appears only on Fiverr/Upwork badges and review tags. It is never a general UI colour.

rules.name: The Token-Only Rule
rules.body: Colours come from the :root variables (var(--main-color), rgba(var(--main-color-rgb), 0.15), var(--black-color)) or this list. Never add new hues, slate/zinc greys or purple/blue gradients. Note that --color-two-rgb is wrong in the CSS (a template leftover), so write 198, 228, 90 for alpha lime.

rules.name: The Three Families Rule
rules.body: Outfit for headings, Manrope for everything readable, Raleway only for hollow decoration. Never add a fourth family (no Inter, Roboto, system-ui or monospace UI text).

rules.name: The One H1 Rule
rules.body: Each page has exactly one h1. Hero slides 2–3 and marquee words are styled divs that look like headings but are not.

rules.name: The Contrast Before Shadow Rule
rules.body: If a block needs to stand apart, first try a section-colour change (white ↔ near-black). Only then reach for an ambient shadow, and never a hard, dark or coloured drop shadow other than the green glow.

dos: Do use the forest → lime 90° gradient for primary actions and brand moments, reversed on hover.
Do keep geometry very round: 50px pills for buttons and fields, 150px capsules for CTA bars and service cards, 50% circles for icons.
Do alternate white and near-black blocks to create rhythm and depth before reaching for shadows.
Do open sections with the eyebrow-plus-dots section title and an Outfit headline.
Do reuse existing components and extend them with modifier classes (.cta-one.style-three) instead of forking them.
Do use Font Awesome 6 icons with aria-hidden="true", inside circular holders where the template does.
Do keep text contrast at 4.5:1 or more (Muted Sage is the floor for normal-size grey text) and wrap every animation in a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce override.
donts: Don't set Fresh Lime as text on light backgrounds, or put small white text over the lime end of the gradient.
Don't use Marketplace Green outside Fiverr/Upwork trust badges and review tags.
Don't add new colours, slate/zinc greys, indigo/violet/blue gradients, or new :root palettes.
Don't add fonts beyond Outfit, Manrope and Raleway.
Don't use emoji as icons, glassmorphism hero cards, bento grids, emoji pill badges, or gradient text on headings.
Don't use sharp-cornered buttons or fields, or hard, dark drop shadows.
Don't make outlined big words or marquee text into heading elements.
Don't use <style> blocks or inline style attributes, except background-image on template decoration elements.
